rules.source: RFC 0007 Q22; RFC 0008 §3.2 (reviews of #996, #998); D2 (PIP-12 parity, review L5 of #1200)
rules.statement: simulate, explain and analyze call the same Engine.evaluate as enforcement, and explanations are built by the enforcing flow. simulate, explain and a shadow window's comparison decide on the documents enforcement reads, by its one rule (ViewDocuments): the platform's, the tenant's, and the app's when the scope has roles in that app or the tenant document decided with (the head, the candidate, or the revision explained) binds one of that app's permission policies to Anyone or a principal; never more. What explain reports as the revisions decided on, and the documents simulate takes a candidate of, are those the view read: a tenant document that does not compile makes a roleless request read no app document. A shadow window's candidate is decided with the failures of the documents it reads, and only those: a tenant candidate that no longer reads an app document is not indeterminate for that document's failure, and one that starts reading an app document that cannot be read or does not compile is (#1410). A candidate of a document that does not compile replaces that failure with itself; one of a document the view could not read is not compared (BASE_MISMATCH). A simulated or explained request that sends a header the documents of its view read with different values is refused 400, as enforcement refuses it before evaluation (PIP-12). An http resource goes through the path normalization every request's path does (PathNormalizer; RC1-41): a path enforcement answers 400 (a dot segment after one decoding, an empty segment, an encoded separator or a backslash (PIP-14), a malformed escape, over 2,048 characters or 256 per segment) is refused 400, by the one function enforcement's checks use (PathNormalizer.enforceable), and the normalized path, its path parameters removed, is decided; a typed resource is held to the same length bounds. analyze takes its resource the same way. analyze resolves a binding's policy as the engine does: a built-in control-plane policy from the engine's own statements (BuiltinPolicies.CONTROL), never counted opaque (#1401); a break-glass binding of cosec:root is listed as an allow marked break-glass, conditional on its window, with that window. An http action goes through the reading every request's method does (PIP-18), by the same function: a verb with a lower-case letter is refused 400, and http:HEAD is decided, and analyzed, as http:GET.

A stage writes its candidate only over the candidate it read, after checking it still holds the slot, so a stage preempted while it writes never replaces the candidate of the change that took the slot.

Anything but a permit refuses it: 403, or 503 when it cannot be decided. The targets of one change are decided on one confirmation of the control documents, confirmed again once they are decided: a document that moved meanwhile has them decided again, so an operator revoked during a change is refused as by a confirmation before each target, and documents that cannot be confirmed again, or keep moving, refuse it (503).

rules.statement: A change that only narrows, every operation one of: removing a binding of an ALLOW-only policy, making an attachable ALLOW-only policy unattachable, a new DENY-only policy or a new binding of one, none on a policy id the platform also defines, staged by a holder of cosec:skip-shadow, takes a busy staging slot: the holder is made CONFLICTED first, from whichever staged state it is in, and keeps its slot when it cannot be. A READY holder whose revision the chain shows written is settled PUBLISHED by whichever change comes for its slot. A PUBLISHED change that still holds its slot, because releasing it after the head write failed, is settled by publishing it again: the slot is released and the publish recorded once, by the call that released it, and no revision is written (#1386). A publish goes on only while its change holds the slot, checked again right before its head write; the change that took a slot and finds the head its holder wrote over the same base records why it failed. Any other change waits (409).

rules.statement: The history of a document is the chain of its head. A revision index is returned only when its last entry is the head's (revision and digest) and each entry above the lowest names, as its parent, the digest of the entry below it; otherwise it is rebuilt from the head's records, replacing only an entry still as the walk compared it, and nothing below the retention floor; an entry that cannot be shown to be on the chain (below a record the walk could not read) is not returned. The write path never replaces a listed revision number that has another digest; the digests a rebuild replaces are left to reclamation, which never deletes a digest the history lists, and the rebuild is logged once with the key and each revision's dropped and kept digest.

A document not published yet is not compared. MERGE removes nothing and proposes on the head.

rules.statement: An :apply with MERGE whose file leaves out entries of the head keeps them, and its change carries one WARNING finding (check OPERATION) per section ($.policies, $.bindings, $.roles, $.rateLimits) that names the kept ids and says that REPLACE removes them. A REPLACE carries none: what it removes are its operations.

rules.statement: A change to the platform document, the platform tenant's document or the control app's document is checked for whether its operator could still reach the control plane once its candidate is in place, decided by the engine on the candidate: the request in progress as the pipeline decided it, and cosec:publish on the document in the control app. A change that would keep its operator out carries a V4 WARNING finding at proposal; at publish, checked for the publisher, it is refused with 422 unless the publisher acknowledges it ("lockout": true), and the message says how to acknowledge and that the way back is cosec-migrate restore. An acknowledged lock-out stays on the published change with who acknowledged it. Only the operator's own way back is checked, with the facts of the request in progress.

A member added to the document format is placed in one of the three or a test fails, so no difference in it diffs as nothing.

rules.statement: The platform's limits set entry budgets: the policies, statements, bindings to roles and bindings to Anyone one document holds (by default 10,000, 20,000, 10,000 and 1,000). The control plane holds every candidate it checks to them, on propose, apply, rollback, rebase and publish: for every budget, the new count is at most the larger of the limit and the old count (that of the head the candidate replaces), with a warning finding naming each count still over; anything that raises an over-budget count is refused, with a 4xx finding naming the budget, the count and the limit, never a 500. Neither the compiler nor a host enforces a budget: a stored document over one keeps being served. cosec-migrate reports a converted document over a default budget as a warning naming the budget, the count and the limit, and writes it.

rules.statement: A change a client proposes carries at most the platform's limits.maxChangeOperations operations (20,000 by default): a larger one is refused 400, naming the count and the limit, before any operation is authorized or applied. An apply and a rollback are not held to it: their operations are derived from a document, which the entry budgets bound (CTL-40). The control routes read at most cosec.control.http.max-body-size of a request's body (10 MB by default) on WebMvc and WebFlux alike, and answer a larger one 400 without asking the control plane.
guards: control:EntryBudgetsTest#a client's change carries at most maxChangeOperations operations, an apply is not held to it
spring-boot:ControlBodyLimitTest#a body within the limit reaches the control plane on both stacks, a larger one is a 400 that never does
spring-boot:ControlBodyLimitTest#the limit is 10 MB by default

rules.source: RFC 0007 §5.8; design B of the back-references, beta.5 (#1729)
rules.statement: A back-reference set that cannot be read, a value in the format before 8.0.0-beta.5 included, fails closed: a read throws naming cosec-migrate repair-references, a check that needs it refuses the change (503), a head write that needs it is not made, and no member is added to or removed from it. Every read of a set asks Redis: the sets of record keep no local copy a read could answer from (local-max-age and degraded-local-max-age locked to 1 ns).
guards: control:ChangesB1Test#back-references that cannot be read refuse a platform id and block a removal - CTL-42
control:RevisionsTest#a back-reference set that cannot be read blocks the platform removing its policy - CTL-42
cocache:CoCacheControlStoreTest#a back-reference value in the format before beta 5 fails closed, naming the repair
cocache:CacheTtlPolicyTest#setOfRecordCachesNeverExpireAndKeepNoLocalCopy
cocache:SetOfRecordReadTest#every read of a back-reference set asks Redis, even in the millisecond its copy was filled in
cocache:SetOfRecordReadTest#the same loop over a set kept locally misses the member, so the test above can fail

rules.source: RFC 0007 §5.8; design B of the back-references, beta.5 (#1729)
rules.statement: A removal of a platform policy is blocked by a referrer unless every entry of it says it defines the id itself, read from the entries and never a head; an entry a later revision or a lost race left that says it refers errs towards blocking, until its tenant's next publish or repair-references removes it. Every referrer of an app's policy blocks its removal. An addition of a platform policy is blocked by every tenant with an entry for that id, whether it defines or binds it, each confirmed by reading its head: a tenant whose head no longer uses the id does not block, and one whose head cannot be read does (503).
guards: control:ReferenceFlagsTest#an addition is blocked by a tenant that defines the id
control:ReferenceFlagsTest#an addition is blocked by a tenant that binds the id, at the check and at publish
control:ReferenceFlagsTest#a stale entry does not block an addition, since the head is read to confirm it
control:ReferenceFlagsTest#a removal is blocked unless every entry of a referrer defines the id
control:AppPermissionReferencesTest#an app's removal check reads no tenant's head

rules.source: RFC 0007 §5.8; design B of the back-references, beta.5 (#1729)
rules.statement: What a tenant's publish reads and writes does not depend on how many other documents refer to the same policies, for a reference it adds and for one it drops alike: it records what it adds in its own revision index before adding one member per reference, and drops exactly the members that record holds, without reading the sets.
guards: control:PublishCostTest#a tenant's publish that adds a reference costs the same at 10 and at 400 referrers
control:PublishCostTest#a tenant's publish that drops a reference costs the same at 10 and at 400 referrers

rules.statement: A process's shadow reports and status are written under an id no earlier process used, whatever cosec.authorization.shadow.instance-id is set to, so a restart never replaces an earlier process's cumulative report or erases a CANDIDATE_ERROR it recorded.
guards: spring-boot:ShadowInstanceIdTest#a configured id is a prefix, with a suffix new at every start
spring-boot:ShadowInstanceIdTest#a restart with the same configured id keeps the earlier report

rules.statement: The staged list is a superset of the candidates staged: a stage lists its document and window, one member added unconditionally so concurrent stages of other documents never make it fail, before it writes its candidate, and a listing that fails fails the stage with nothing written; a candidate is withdrawn before its window is unlisted, and a withdrawal that fails leaves it listed. Every shadow pass, under its lease, keeps the list, lists the window of a shadowing change whose candidate is written and not listed, and unlists a window whose document stages no candidate of it once two passes in a row found it so.
guards: control:StagedListTest#a stage lists its window before its candidate, and a withdrawal unlists it after
control:StagedListTest#a listing that fails fails the stage, with nothing staged
control:StagedListTest#the shadow pass keeps the list, lists a staged candidate a lost write left out, and unlists a stale window after a pass of grace
control:StagedListTest#fifty tenants staging at once are all staged and all listed
control:StagedListReconciliationTest#a pass that could not read every change leaves an unnamed candidate staged, and complete passes withdraw it
cocache:StagedListStoreTest#the list is absent until kept, then lists exactly what is added and not removed
cocache:StagedListStoreTest#fifty documents listed and staged at once all land

rules.statement: An app change lists the tenants a widened permission policy reaches as one informational entry per policy, counted from the back-reference index, without reading a tenant document; that entry never stands in for an escalation that needs approval: only TENANT_BINDINGS is informational, and an approval must still cover every other escalation.
guards: control:InformationalEscalationTest#only the tenants' entry is informational
control:InformationalEscalationTest#an aggregated tenant entry never stands in for the approval the widening needs
control:ChangesB1Test#widening an app permission policy lists the tenant bindings it widens - RC1-34

rules.source: Review round 2, R2C-25 and R2C-26 (saas-app-change-cost.md); RFC 0007 §7.4.3, §7.5
rules.statement: A grant analysis makes at most its comparison budget of comparisons, spent in the analysis's order, and over it never answers contained: a statement still being compared when the budget runs out is granted, and every fragment it reaches past the budget is unknown (too large to analyze), so what it did not compare needs approval.
guards: control:ComparisonBudgetTest#past the budget a fragment is too large to analyze, never contained
control:ComparisonBudgetTest#a statement still being compared when the budget runs out is granted
control:ComparisonBudgetTest#the same change stops at the same comparison

rules.statement: What the grant analysis skips as unchanged, a policy or a statement it takes as written before, is identical to the previous version in every member the grant depends on: each member of a policy, a statement and the patterns they hold is compared, or listed with why it need not be, and a statement identical to a previous one narrows it, whatever its condition.
guards: control:GrantPolicyMembersTest#every member is compared or listed with a reason
control:GrantPolicyMembersTest#a statement's condition removed is analysed
control:GrantPolicyMembersTest#a path pattern made case insensitive is analysed
control:GrantPolicyMembersTest#a path pattern matched on the raw path is analysed
control:GrantPolicyMembersTest#a policy condition removed, or the policy made attachable, is analysed
control:GrantReflexivityTest#a twin policy is the same policy, and each twin statement narrows its previous one

rules.statement: simulate and explain name a statement (its policy, index and name, and in the trace its effect and whether it matched) only to a caller who may read the document that defines its policy, whichever document the binding it applied through lives in: a tenant's binding to a platform policy or to an app's permission policy shows a tenant administrator neither the statement that decided nor any of that policy's statements in the trace, which are counted as redacted. A caller who may read the defining document is told them.
guards: control:DecisionQueriesTest#a tenant administrator does not see the statements of a platform policy their binding points to
control:DecisionQueriesTest#a tenant administrator does not see the statements of an app policy their binding points to
control:DecisionQueriesTest#a platform operator still sees them, and a tenant administrator their own tenant's statements

rules.statement: No store failure reads as an empty answer: over a control store that cannot answer, every control route answers 503 without detail to a caller it is for, and both maintenance passes do nothing that pass; a stored value that does not decode is a 500, never a 400 or an absence.
guards: control:StoreOutageTest#every route answers 503 without detail while the store cannot answer
control:StoreOutageTest#both maintenance passes do nothing while the store cannot answer
cocache:CoCacheControlStoreTest#a set that fails to read for another reason does not name the repair

rules.statement: Every record the control plane and its hosts store carries a format and is read by one rule: a record without one is format 1; of a known format, members this version does not know are ignored; a later format is refused, as a format error, never read as absent. Policy documents, API keys and back-reference members are decision inputs and stay strict. A wrong value of any stored record is a format error, never an argument or JSON error a store would read as an outage.
guards: cocache:StoredRecordsTest#every stored codec is listed
cocache:StoredRecordsTest#a wrong value of every stored record is a format error
cocache:StoredRecordsTest#every record with a format ignores what it does not know, reads one without a format, and refuses a later one
control:ChangeRequestCodecMessageTest#unknown members are ignored, and never quoted, by the reader's rule - CTL-53
document:ShadowCodecMessageTest#unknown members are ignored, and never quoted, by the reader's rule - CTL-53

rules.statement: The open-change sets are a superset of the open changes: a change is added to its document's set and its state's before each write of it and removed after from what no longer applies; they are trusted only once kept and while no open-change list of the format before 8.0.0-beta.5 exists, so until then no revision is reclaimed and the listing is refused.
guards: cocache:CoCacheControlStoreTest#the open-change sets are not kept while the old list is there, whatever they hold
cocache:CoCacheControlStoreTest#a new store is kept from the first keep
cocache:CoCacheControlStoreTest#members a write left behind are dropped by the next read
cocache:CoCacheControlStoreTest#a listed change that is missing stays until the grace has passed
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#a reader between a write's listing and its record keeps the new member
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#a write that unlists late takes out only the record it replaced
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#a change that comes back to a state keeps its member when the write that left it unlists late
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#writers that pause before they unlist never take a later write's member
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#a stale member goes after the grace and the current one stays, the change listed once
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#a member a lost write left is never listed, and goes after the grace
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#a member without a digest is read as stale
cocache:OpenChangeSetsRaceTest#concurrent writers that bring changes back to their states leave every open change listed
control:OpenChangeListingTest#while the old list is there the listing is a 503 and nothing is reclaimed - CTL-54

rules.statement: A listing of open changes shows a change only if reading it by id would show it to the caller, leaves out what the caller may not see before the page is cut, and tells nothing of what it leaves out.
guards: control:OpenChangeListingTest#another tenant's changes are left out, and the page says nothing of them - CTL-55
control:OpenChangeListingTest#a listing by document or by state shows the caller's tenant only, a summary of each change
control:OpenChangeListingTest#a page is cut after what the caller may see, and the next one goes on from it
control:OpenChangeListingTest#a cursor names only a change the caller sees, and only when one follows it - CTL-55
control:OpenChangeListingTest#a member of the tenant who may not read its changes sees none, a viewer sees them - CTL-55

rules.statement: An instance reads the staged list off the request path and, with a list, reads a candidate only for a document it lists and samples only a request whose view reads a listed document; with nothing listed it samples nothing and reads no candidate. Without a list kept (no list, or a control plane that does not keep one) it reads every candidate by its key and samples as before; a list it cannot read counts as no list, never as nothing staged. The list only gates: a candidate is still read by its key and checked by its window, so a list read late, or kept by no one any more, costs samples and never yields a sample of the wrong candidate, nor a pass.
guards: runtime:StagedDocumentsTest#with no list kept, every document may stage a candidate, read by its key
runtime:StagedDocumentsTest#a list read gates the reads and the samples, and with nothing listed nothing is sampled
runtime:StagedDocumentsTest#a list that cannot be read counts as no list, never as nothing staged
runtime:StagedDocumentsTest#an unlisted document's candidate is not read, and its requests are not sampled
runtime:StagedDocumentsTest#a candidate staged where the list is kept by no one any more gives no sample

rules.statement: No shadow window passes on missing evidence: an instance that reported on a window and has no report is waited for, and at the longest window the window closes insufficient, naming it; it never closes passing on the others' reports.
guards: control:ControlRoundTwoFixesTest#a window whose reporter vanished closes insufficient at the longest window, naming it - CTL-56
control:ControlRoundTwoFixesTest#an instance seen reporting on a window must keep reporting until it closes
control:ControlRoundTwoFixesTest#an unreadable report waits then closes insufficient, a store outage does neither - CTL-56
cocache:ShadowReadingsTest#a listed report that is missing, does not decode, or is another's is that instance's reading
cocache:ShadowReadingsTest#a store that does not answer fails the whole call, never reads as an unreadable report
spi:ShadowValuesTest#the default readings read the reports, and throw where they throw

rules.source: Review round 2, R2C-11 and R2C-13 (review-r2-3-control-storage.md); RFC 0007 §10
rules.statement: The control API answers from a response model of its own: a change answer holds only the members its codec writes, never what the stored record keeps for the store's own work (the heads it was checked with, the instances that reported on its window, the record's format, what an approver held); a decision's closed sets come from one table each, an undecided decision naming the kind of its failure under `cause` and a refused scope its reason under `reason`, never a class's name; and `contract/control/` pins the members, the closed sets and the change kind each route writes to the audit stream.
guards: control:ControlAnswersTest#a change answer holds only what its codec writes, never the record's bookkeeping - CTL-61
control:ControlAnswersTest#a refused scope says why under reason, never under cause - CTL-61
control:ControlAnswersTest#an undecided decision names the kind of its cause from one table, never a class's name - CTL-61
control:ClientContractTest#a change answer holds exactly the members of its contract file
control:ClientContractTest#a listed change holds exactly the members of its contract file
control:ClientContractTest#the closed sets of the control API are those of their contract file
control:ClientContractTest#each route that moves a change writes the change kinds of its contract file

rules.statement: A revision's propagation counts, of the instances that reported a status in the last minute, those that hold the document at any revision and those of them that installed the revision or a later one, and says when it read the statuses: no instance is behind when every instance holding the document installed it, and when none holds it the first request that needs it loads it at the published revision. The statuses are read at most every five seconds, and a read that fails is answered 503, never from an older read.
guards: control:PropagationTest#propagation counts the instances that hold the document, and says when it read them - CTL-62
control:PropagationTest#the statuses are read at most every five seconds, and the answer is as old as that read
control:PropagationTest#a status read that fails is never kept nor answered from an older read - CTL-62
control:ClientContractTest#a propagation answer holds exactly the members of its contract file
